chunks: Ali ibn al-Nu'man narrated to us from Ibn Muskān, from Sulaymān ibn Khālid, from Abū Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

Should I not inform you about Islam: its branch, its root, its summit and its peak? I said, Yes, indeed, may I be your ransom! He said: As for its root, it is prayer; as for its branch, it is alms-tax; as for its summit and peak, it is holy struggle.
ai.seo_question: What are the root, branch, and peak of Islam according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Kitab al-Zuhd*, Abū Ja'far (Imam al-Baqir) employs an agricultural metaphor to delineate the hierarchy of Islamic obligations, positioning prayer as the foundational root, zakat as the sustaining branch, and jihad as the ultimate fruit or peak. This structure reflects the Shia scholarly understanding of jihad not merely as warfare but as the culmination of spiritual and material devotion, elevating it to the status of the faith's highest expression.

en.shaykh-tahir-ridha-jaffer: 3.ʿAlī ibn al-Nuʿmān narrated to us from Ibn Muskān, from Sulaymān ibn Khālid, from Abū Jaʿfar (a) who said, “

Should I not inform you about Islam: its branch, its root, its summit and its peak?” I said, “Yes, indeed, may I be your ransom!” He said, “As for its root [and foundation], it is prayer; as for its branch, it is zakāt (alms-tax); as for its summit and peak, it is jihād (holy struggle).”
